newsitem.title: FRANCE: Twenty pct of France Telecom offer in Apr 97-paper.
newsitem.headline: Twenty pct of France Telecom offer in Apr 97-paper.

text.p: About 20 percent of France Telecom will be offered for sale to the public in the second half of April 1997, Telecommunications Minister Francois Fillon said in a interview published in La Tribune Desfosses on Tuesday.

Fillon also said in the interview that he hopes a third major telephone operator will emerge in France to compete with France Telecom and Cegetel, the telephone operator being set up by Generale des Eaux in partnership with British Telecom, SBC Communications Inc and Mannesmann AG.

Fillon said 20 percent of France Telecom's capital was a "financially high" slice to reserve for a cross shareholding with Deutsche Telekom, but added that it was too soon to tell what the right amount should be.

"Before deciding on the cross shareholding with Deutsche Telekom, we must know the value of the German and French operators. Taking into account the foreseeable value of the companies, 20 percent seems to me financially high," he said.
Fillon said employees would be able to hold 10 percent of the company and that the government is not trying to build a stable core of shareholders as it has done with other companies.
